skill.name: seaborn
skill.description: Guides Seaborn statistical visualization for exploratory analysis and publication figures, including plot selection, semantic mappings, faceting, regression, distributions, matrices, themes, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Create clear statistical graphics with Seaborn, from quick exploration to publication-ready multi-panel figures.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 201 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and ordinary Seaborn plotting terms. The skill contains documentation and Python visualization examples, with no shell execution, reconnaissance, prompt injection, credential access, or exfiltration intent. The quick-start sample may download Seaborn's public tips dataset, but it does not send user data.

The `seaborn.objects` interface provides a declarative, composable API similar to ggplot2. Build vis
- `lineplot()` - Show trends and changes (automatically aggregates and computes CI)
- `hue` - Color encoding for additional categorical/continuous variable
- `histplot()` - Bar-based frequency distributions with flexible binning
- `kdeplot()` - Smooth density estimates using Gaussian kernels
- `ecdfplot()` - Empirical cumulative distribution (no parameters to tune)
- `displot()` - Figure-level interface for univariate and bivariate distributions
- `pairplot()` - Matrix of pairwise relationships across dataset
- `stripplot()` - Points with jitter to show all observations
- `regplot()` - Axes-level regression plot with scatter + fit line
- `residplot()` - Residual plot for assessing model fit
- `robust` - Use robust regression (less sensitive to outliers)
- `center` - Value at colormap center (for diverging colormaps)
Create subplots based on categorical variables. Most useful when called through figure-level functio

content.value_statement: Choosing appropriate statistical plots and settings can be difficult when datasets contain multiple variable types and groups. This skill guides Seaborn plot selection, composition, styling, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Seaborn plot types for relational, distributional, categorical, regression, and matrix data.
Explains axes-level, figure-level, and seaborn.objects interfaces.
Guides semantic mappings, faceting, palettes, themes, and statistical estimators.
Describes long-form and wide-form data preparation.
Provides patterns for exploratory, publication, multi-panel, and time-series figures.
Diagnoses common issues involving legends, labels, figure size, colors, and KDE bandwidth.
limitations: Requires Python with Seaborn, Matplotlib, pandas, and any analysis-specific dependencies installed.
Does not inspect datasets automatically; users must provide schemas, samples, or relevant column details.
Generated plots still require validation for statistical correctness, accessibility, and publication requirements.
Version-specific Seaborn APIs may differ from the reference material.

use_cases.title: Explore a New Dataset
use_cases.description: Select relationship, distribution, and correlation plots that reveal structure, outliers, and group differences.

use_cases.title: Prepare Publication Figures
use_cases.description: Design clear multi-panel figures with controlled themes, labels, uncertainty, palettes, and export settings.

use_cases.title: Build Reusable Plotting Workflows
use_cases.description: Choose compatible Seaborn interfaces and Matplotlib integration patterns for repeatable visualization functions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Basic Plot
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Seaborn plot for [goal] using DataFrame [name]. Columns: [columns]. Recommend the plot type and explain each mapping.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Groups
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [metric] across [category] and [group]. Use an accessible palette, display uncertainty appropriately, and include clear labels.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Faceted Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a faceted analysis of [dataset] using [row] and [column] groups. Control ordering, scales, legends, and statistical estimation.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Publication Figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a publication figure for [research question] with Seaborn objects or Matplotlib integration. Specify transformations, layers, layout, export settings, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Show how total bill relates to tip, separated by day.
output_examples.output: Recommended a scatter plot with bill and tip axes, day color encoding, an accessible palette, clear labels, and an optional regression view.

output_examples.input: Compare response distributions across treatment groups.
output_examples.output: Recommended a violin or box plot with visible observations, ordered groups, uncertainty guidance, and notes about sample size and skew.
Outlined a masked correlation heatmap with a centered diverging palette, readable annotations, square cells, descriptive labels, and vector export.

best_practices: Use tidy, long-form data with meaningful column names whenever possible.
Match plot type and statistical estimator to the data structure and analytical question.
Validate labels, uncertainty, accessibility, and export quality before sharing a figure.
anti_patterns: Do not use color as the only encoding when accessibility matters.
Do not accept automatic aggregation or confidence intervals without checking their statistical meaning.
Do not overload a figure with excessive categories, facets, or semantic mappings.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers plot selection, Seaborn interfaces, statistical mappings, faceting, themes, publication workflows, and common troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does it install Seaborn?
faq.answer: No. Install Seaborn, Matplotlib, pandas, and required statistical dependencies in your Python environment.

faq.question: Can it analyze my data automatically?
faq.answer: No. Provide column names, data types, sample values, and the analytical question for useful guidance.

faq.question: Does it support the seaborn.objects interface?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains declarative plots, marks, transformations, scales, layouts, and related composition patterns.

faq.question: Can it help create publication figures?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance for themes, labels, multi-panel layouts, uncertainty, resolution, and vector export.

faq.question: Does it guarantee statistical correctness?
faq.answer: No. Review estimators, uncertainty methods, transformations, sample sizes, and assumptions with appropriate domain expertise.
